name: promise
axes: X forward, Y left, Z up

provenance.source: NASA PROMISE interactive GLB, November 7 2026 release
provenance.operation: All visible geometry, at full resolution. Rotate to ROS FLU and keep NASA materials and corner normals. Split the one-piece rocker-bogie meshes into body, rocker and bogie parts and the mast at z=1.875 m into yaw and pitch parts. Joint axes fitted to NASA hub bearing rings; wheels turned 0.5-0.7 degrees so their axles match the +Y spin joints.

Recess into the original white enclosure, near its front face; rotate +22.5 degrees around ROS +Y so forward rays point down. Hollow the box and cut a 150 x 92 mm front aperture; replace roof bracket with an internal tilted cradle. User-requested modification, not NASA flight CAD.

notes: Masses, inertias, joint limits, actuator gains, friction and optical calibration are estimates, not NASA flight parameters.
All visible rover geometry is NASA's public PROMISE visualization. TRIDENT is fixed in its stowed driving pose.
Tread geometry is visual; wheel contact is a smooth cylinder. No deformable regolith model.
OS1 Rev8 is a user-requested turret sensor substitution, not a NASA flight hardware claim.

lidar.name: os1
lidar.calibration: Uniform elevation, zero azimuth offsets, approximate optical origin; not device-calibrated beam intrinsics.
lidar.sampling: Instantaneous full frame, single geometric return; no packet transport, reflectivity, native RGB, dual returns or calibrated noise.

enclosure.note: True open aperture and hollow cavity; no glass cover. Original enclosure footprint and four camera meshes retained.

lidar.installation: Recessed inside white mast head, behind a front aperture. Enclosure blocks most side/rear directions; do not interpret the native 360-degree scan grid as unobstructed coverage.

head_visibility.scope: Only geometry rigidly attached to head_pitch_link; excludes OS1 case. Other rover/environment occlusion is dynamic.
